newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes up on mild speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes up on mild speculation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates ended 55 basis points higher at 22.80 percent due to speculative trade late in the day after a stable session, dealers said.
Paper was in supply due to the speculation, dealers said, but added that overnight rates were still stable at between 22 and 23 percent.
"Indeed it may be said that we're slightly below last week's rates. We have touched the 23 percent mark, but forcibly and at low volume," a trader said.
Dealers added that they had reined in speculation as government paper was evenly distributed between them.
"Paper's very evenly shared out and that keeps the market on an even keel," one of them said.
Traders said that liquidity shortages, initially estimated at 2.002 billion pesos, were increased by 1.9 billion pesos leaving the system prior to the weekend.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed 20 basis points down at 24.50 percent.
Liquidity shortages on Friday were expected to arise from total credit maturities of 3.688 billion pesos, and an estimated additional outflow of 1.3 billion pesos prior to the weekend.
